items.prompt: Two std::error_code objects report value()==5, but a.category() and b.category() are different categories. What can a portable caller infer from the equal numbers alone?

options.text: a==b, because error_code equality only compares the stored integer.
options.why: error_code equality includes category; equal integer values alone do not establish equal codes.

options.text: Equal numbers alone do not establish equal error meanings.
options.why: The category supplies meaning to its numeric code. A portable std::errc condition can be tested through category equivalence rules rather than raw numbers.

options.text: Both must be equivalent to std::errc::io_error.
options.why: A raw value is not a universal std::errc encoding across categories and platforms.

options.text: Comparing a code to a portable std::errc condition is always invalid.
options.why: The standard supports portable error-condition comparisons; the mistake is discarding the category and comparing raw numbers.

items.explanation: The category supplies meaning to its numeric code. A portable std::errc condition can be tested through category equivalence rules rather than raw numbers.
